A3.1.heading: \section{Inputs, equivalence and complete finite evidence} The search uses the complete subgroup-class and maximal-inclusion data for $J_2$ supplied by GAP's TomLib. It does not use a list of known geometries. For every subgroup $B$, conjugate inclusions are reconstructed by UD.Transport. The action of $N_{J_2}(B)$ on the actual panel subgroups may have a kernel; replacing it by its permutation image preserves the orbits because every image element has an acting lift. All incidence and subgroup tests are still performed on the original subgroups. No faithfulness of this auxiliary action is assumed.

A3.2.heading: \section{The exact source boundary} The source's main article, on printed pages 79--80, also displays rank-four diagrams, local annotations, full geometric automorphism and correlation groups, and a doubling relation between examples. These assertions are not all recovered here. They are printed-body omissions, not merely missing annotations in an external supplement. They remain excluded from the fixed principal census contract. No new historical classification or additional source credit is claimed.

Support.1.heading: \section{Admissible extensions with prescribed support} Let a finite group $A$ act on finite sets $Z$ and $E$, and let $p:Z\to E$ be equivariant. Let $R\subseteq Z$ be invariant; it is the set passing the application's admissibility tests. Suppose a finite poset $L$ with greatest element $1$ has an $A$-action by order automorphisms and an equivariant map $s:R\to L$. Write $R_l=\{z\in R:s(z)\le l\}$. The individual sets $R_l$ need not be invariant. Choose one $e$ in each $A$-orbit in $p(R)$, and put $R(e)=R\cap p^{-1}(e)$.
